title: Cover: your introduction
narration:
I’m Yuwei Zhang from Team GreenAcorn. My background is in pathology and epidemiology.

Pathology taught me to look closely at disease. Epidemiology taught me to see patterns across communities. Patients reminded me that neither view tells the whole story.

PathwayAI connects those dots.

Let me show you.

title: Start with the complete pathway
narration: Start before a bite. Continue through care, burden, and community action.

title: Plan before going outdoors
navigation: Plan time outdoors → Your outdoor plan
narration: Choose where and when you will be outdoors, and what you plan to do. Prevention starts with preparation.

title: Prepare, check, and respond
navigation: Learn & Prevent → Generate My Outdoor Tick-Prevention Plan
narration: Prepare protective clothing and an EPA-registered repellent. Follow product instructions. Afterwards, check your body, clothing, gear, and pets. Shower within two hours. These steps reduce risk; they cannot guarantee protection.

title: After a tick bite
navigation: After a tick bite → Remove → Record → Seek advice
narration: If a tick is attached, grasp close to the skin with fine-tipped tweezers and pull upward steadily. Record when and where. Some high-risk bites need prompt clinical advice. Do not wait for symptoms if you need prevention advice.

title: Record when and where
navigation: Prepare for care → Tick encounter details
narration: Keep the date and exposure location. These may differ from where you live or need care.

title: Tell the story once
navigation: Prepare for care → Tell us what happened → Organize My Story
narration: Here is a fictional person preparing for care after feeling unwell. They write a short story, including costs and help received. PathwayAI organizes details they can check, correct, and download.

title: Prepare questions about testing
navigation: Care & Support → Lyme tests → Before the test
narration: The testing guide helps people ask about timing, their complete report, and costs. It prepares a conversation; it does not diagnose.

title: Include daily life and caregiver experience
navigation: Care & Support → Daily life and caregiver experience
narration: Caregivers can help describe daily-life difficulties. We label their observations and keep their own experience separate. Partial answers are welcome.

title: Review payments, work and unpaid help
navigation: Care & Support → Review and download your visit and burden card
narration: This fictional person paid one hundred eighty dollars for care and forty-five for travel. That is two hundred twenty-five dollars. Three workdays and eight caregiver hours stay separate. Unknown answers stay unknown.

title: Prepare a request for support
navigation: Care & Support → Choose the help you need → Getting to care
narration: Now the record supports a next step: a transport request asking about eligibility, cost, booking, and the return trip. The person chooses what to share.

title: Prepare for a benefits conversation
navigation: Care & Support → Prepare for a benefits conversation
narration: Benefits preparation helps organize questions and records for food assistance or disability support. Agencies decide eligibility. Nothing is submitted automatically.

title: Compare county evidence
navigation: Community Burden & Action → Compare Dutchess and Orange
narration: Now compare Dutchess and Orange counties. CDC, Census, and HRSA data add context alongside New York surveillance and published research. County averages do not describe every person.

title: Explore a cost illustration
navigation: Community → Estimated community cost: Dutchess and Orange
narration: This illustration multiplies reported cases by a study mean: about four point one million dollars, in twenty sixteen dollars. It is not measured county spending.

title: Connect needs with possible actions
narration: What could a community do next? Patients, caregivers, and willing partners could review transport barriers, choose a feasible response, and track rides completed, appointments attended, and unmet needs.

title: Summarize comparable reports
navigation: Community → See how comparable patient reports could be summarized
narration: These six records are invented. Five have usable answers; one leaves fields unknown. Comparable reports could inform planning, but voluntary reports cannot represent everyone.

title: Ask about the public evidence
navigation: Community → Ask AI about the public evidence
narration:
Optional AI explains curated public evidence without receiving private patient cards. Story AI requires permission; the local organizer works without it.

AI can organize information, but people review its meaning. Data can reveal patterns, but cannot replace lived experience.

title: Patients and people remain at the center
narration:
Models explore possibilities; people remain responsible for decisions. The patient stays at the center.

To patients, caregivers, advocates, and experts: thank you. Your experiences and guidance helped make PathwayAI possible.

Making the Hidden Patient Journey Visible—and Actionable.
